nodes.summary: Let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be a map. For $u : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, $n \ge 1$ and $x \in \alpha$, write $A_n u(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} u(T^k x)$ for the $n$-th Birkhoff average of $u$ at $x$, and $A_0 u(x) = 0$. If $u, v : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $u(y) \le v(y)$ for every $y \in \alpha$, then $A_n u(x) \le A_n v(x)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $x \in \alpha$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of Birkhoff averages

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be ergodic with respect to $\mu$ (in particular $T$ preserves $\mu$), and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. For $n \ge 1$ let $A_n g(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ be the Birkhoff averages of $g$. Then $\int \left| A_n g(x) - \int g \, d\mu \right| d\mu(x) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$; that is,…
nodes.title: Birkhoff's ergodic theorem in $L^1$ (ergodic case)

nodes.summary: The Birkhoff limit is the conditional expectation of `f` given the invariant σ-algebra.
nodes.title: Birkhoff limit is a conditional expectation on invariant sets

nodes.summary: For ergodic `T` on a probability space the Birkhoff limit is the constant `∫ f dμ`; this is `MathlibExt.Dynamics.Ergodic.BirkhoffWanted.birkhoff_pointwise_ergodic` combined with `tendsto_birkhoffAverage_ae`.
nodes.title: Birkhoff limit of an ergodic map is the space average

nodes.summary: The limit of the Birkhoff averages of `f` (defined as `f*` cast to `ℝ`; it is the limit almost everywhere by `tendsto_birkhoffAverage_ae`).
nodes.title: Birkhoff limit of a function

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be ergodic with respect to $\mu$ (in particular $T$ preserves $\mu$), and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. Then for $\mu$-almost every $x \in \alpha$, the Birkhoff averages $\frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ converge to $\int g \, d\mu$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Birkhoff pointwise ergodic theorem (ergodic case)

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space. For every map $T : \alpha \to \alpha$, every function $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ and every real number $c$, the preimage under $T$ of the maximal divergence set of $T$, $g$ and $c$ equals that set.
nodes.title: Invariance of the maximal divergence set

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space, $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ a map, $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ a function and $c$ a real number. For every natural number $k$ and every $x \in \alpha$, the point $T^k x$ lies in the maximal divergence set of $T$, $g$ and $c$ if and only if $x$ does.
nodes.title: Invariance of the maximal divergence set under iterates

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be measurable. Then for every real number $c$, the maximal divergence set of $T$, $g$ and $c$ is a measurable set.
nodes.title: Measurability of the maximal divergence set

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space, $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ a map, $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ a function, $c$ a real number and $x \in \alpha$. Then $x$ lies in the maximal divergence set of $T$, $g$ and $c$ if and only if there is a rational number $q > c$ such that for every natural number $N$ there is a natural number $n \ge N$ with $n q < \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$.
nodes.title: Membership in the maximal divergence set

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space, $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ a map, $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ a function and $c$ a real number. The maximal divergence set of $T$, $g$ and $c$ is the set of points $x \in \alpha$ for which there is a rational number $q > c$ such that $n q < \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ for infinitely many natural numbers $n$.
nodes.title: Maximal divergence set

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space, $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ a map, $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ a function, $c$ a real number, and $D \subseteq \alpha$ a set such that for every natural number $k$ and every $x \in \alpha$, $T^k x \in D$ if and only if $x \in D$. Let $h : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $h(y) = g(y) - c$ for $y \in D$ and $h(y) = 0$ for $y \notin D$. Then for every $x \in D$ and every natural number…
nodes.title: Birkhoff sums of a function cut off to an invariant set, inside the set

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space, $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ a map, $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ a function, $c$ a real number, and $D \subseteq \alpha$ a set such that for every natural number $k$ and every $x \in \alpha$, $T^k x \in D$ if and only if $x \in D$. Let $h : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $h(y) = g(y) - c$ for $y \in D$ and $h(y) = 0$ for $y \notin D$. Then for every $x \notin D$ and every natural…
nodes.title: Birkhoff sums of a function cut off to an invariant set, outside the set

nodes.summary: Birkhoff averages are `L¹`-contractions. See also `MathlibExt.Probability.BirkhoffErgodicL1.integral_norm_birkhoffAverage_sub_le`, the same bound for differences, stated with integrals of norms.
nodes.title: Birkhoff averages are L1 contractions

nodes.summary: The upper limit of the Birkhoff averages is `T`-invariant.
nodes.title: Upper limit of Birkhoff averages is invariant

nodes.summary: The lower limit `liminf_n A_n f x` of the Birkhoff averages, in `EReal`.
nodes.title: Lower limit of Birkhoff averages

nodes.summary: The upper limit `limsup_n A_n f x` of the Birkhoff averages, in `EReal`.
nodes.title: Upper limit of Birkhoff averages

nodes.summary: Maximal ergodic theorem (E. Hopf, 1954), in the finite form of A. M. Garsia, *A simple proof of E. Hopf's maximal ergodic theorem*, 1965: for measure-preserving `T` and integrable `f`, the integral of `f` over `{max_{1 ≤ n ≤ N} S_n f > 0}` is nonnegative. See also `MathlibExt.Dynamics.Ergodic.BirkhoffWanted.maximal_ergodic`, the limiting form for measurable `f`.
nodes.title: Maximal ergodic theorem

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ the Birkhoff average $x \mapsto \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ is $\mu$-integrable (for $n = 0$ it is the zero function).
nodes.title: Integrability of Birkhoff averages

nodes.summary: The Birkhoff limit of an integrable function is integrable.
nodes.title: Integrability of the Birkhoff limit

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ the Birkhoff sum $x \mapsto \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ is $\mu$-integrable.
nodes.title: Integrability of Birkhoff sums

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $u : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. Then for every $n \ge 1$, $\int \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} u(T^k x) \, d\mu(x) = \int u \, d\mu$.
nodes.title: Birkhoff averages preserve the integral

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $u : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. Then for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, writing $T^k$ for the $k$-th iterate of $T$, we have $\int u(T^k x) \, d\mu(x) = \int u \, d\mu$.
nodes.title: Invariance of the integral under iterates

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $g, h : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. For a function $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ and $n \ge 1$ write $A_n f(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(T^k x)$, and $A_0 f = 0$. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $\int |A_n g(x) - A_n h(x)| \, d\mu(x) \le \int |g(x) - h(x)| \, d\mu(x)$.
nodes.title: Birkhoff averages are $L^1$-contractions

nodes.summary: `IsInvariantSet T E` is the condition `T ⁻¹' E = E` used by Mathlib's `PreErgodic` and `MeasurableSpace.invariants`.
nodes.title: Invariant set as a set equal to its preimage

nodes.summary: `E` is invariant under `T`: `x ∈ E ↔ T x ∈ E`, i.e. `T ⁻¹' E = E` (see `isInvariantSet_iff_preimage_eq`).
nodes.title: Invariant set of a map

nodes.summary: An invariant set is invariant under every iterate.
nodes.title: Invariant set is invariant under every iterate

nodes.summary: The invariant set `{f_* < a} ∩ {b < f*}` where the Birkhoff averages oscillate across `[a, b]`.
nodes.title: Oscillation set of Birkhoff averages

nodes.summary: The maximal Birkhoff sum `max_{1 ≤ n ≤ N} ∑_{k<n} f (T^[k] x)` over the first `N` times.
nodes.title: Maximal Birkhoff partial sum

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be measurable and $\mu$-integrable. For a natural number $n$ write $S_n f(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(T^k x)$. Then the integral of $f$ with respect to $\mu$ over the set of points $x \in \alpha$ such that $S_n f(x) > 0$ for some natural number $n$ is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Hopf maximal ergodic theorem

nodes.summary: For `a < b` the oscillation set `levelSet T f a b` is null.
nodes.title: Oscillation set of Birkhoff averages is null

nodes.summary: Let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be a map. For $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ and $n \ge 1$ write $A_n f(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(T^k x)$ for the $n$-th Birkhoff average of $f$, and $A_0 f = 0$. Then for every $u : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $x \in \alpha$, writing $|u|$ for the function $y \mapsto |u(y)|$, we have $|A_n u(x)| \le A_n |u|(x)$.
nodes.title: Triangle inequality for Birkhoff averages

nodes.summary: Let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be a map, let $M \ge 0$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $|g(x)| \le M$ for every $x \in \alpha$. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $x \in \alpha$, the Birkhoff average $\frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ (taken to be $0$ for $n = 0$) has absolute value at most $M$.
nodes.title: Birkhoff averages of a bounded function are bounded

nodes.summary: On every measurable invariant set `E`, `∫_E birkhoffLimit T f dμ = ∫_E f dμ`.
nodes.title: Birkhoff limit preserves integrals over invariant sets

nodes.summary: The maximal inequality on an invariant set: if every point of the invariant set `E` has some positive Birkhoff sum of `g`, then `∫_E g dμ ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Maximal ergodic inequality on an invariant set

nodes.summary: The Birkhoff averages of an integrable `f` converge a.e. to `birkhoffLimit T f`.
nodes.title: Birkhoff averages converge almost everywhere to the Birkhoff limit

nodes.summary: Birkhoff's pointwise ergodic theorem (G. D. Birkhoff, *Proof of the ergodic theorem*, 1931): for `T` preserving a finite measure `μ` and integrable `f`, the averages `(1/n) ∑_{k<n} f ∘ T^k` converge `μ`-a.e. to `μ[f | MeasurableSpace.invariants T]`. See also `MathlibExt.Dynamics.Ergodic.BirkhoffWanted.birkhoff_pointwise_ergodic`, the ergodic case, and `birkhoffLimit_ae_eq_integral_of_ergodic`.
nodes.title: Birkhoff's pointwise ergodic theorem

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be ergodic with respect to $\mu$ (in particular $T$ preserves $\mu$), let $M \ge 0$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable with $|g(x)| \le M$ for every $x \in \alpha$. can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
